language_task: Pick up one object from the big bowl and put it inside the small box that is empty.
outcome_evidence: Provisionally, no bowl-to-box transfer is completed in this window. The robot retains an empty orange box throughout, moving it away from and back beside the bowl (left and top, frames 1750, 1800, 1830, 1900 and 1999), rather than acquiring a bowl object. The green and brown objects remain in the bowl (right and left, frames 1900–1999). Completion outside this window is unconfirmed; earlier context is limited to frames 1748–1749, and no later execution is supplied.

failure_annotations.explanation: The robot continues carrying the empty orange box, initially away from the bowl, then back beside it, with further small repositioning motions and pauses instead of acquiring any bowl contents (left and top, frames 1750–1830, 1890–1940 and 1999). The box remains empty and retained while the bowl objects remain available (left and right, frames 1900, 1950 and 1999). Although brief destination positioning could be preparation, this sustained box-handling sequence makes no discernible transfer progress. The supplied context frames 1748–1749 show the same held box, supporting continuity at the start; the behavior may extend beyond either window boundary, and its earlier onset is not established here.
failure_annotations.recovery: Set the held box upright on a clear tabletop area and release it, then grasp one object from inside the bowl, verify retention, and place it into the empty box; no human intervention is visibly needed.
failure_annotations.severity_evidence: No damage, spill, dropped object or meaningful damage risk is established in left, right or top through frame 1999; the visible consequence is failure to perform the requested transfer.
failure_annotations.resetability_evidence: The box remains controlled and the bowl contents remain accessible; the robot can set the box down and proceed without environmental repair or a human reset.
